On 19 November, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in what is a now a landmark judgment of the 21st century on the gravest of all international crimes. The case before the ICJ was brought by The Gambia, a West African nation, in 2019.
Watch ThePrint’s Bantirani Patro explain why the verdict matters, the case timeline, what lies ahead for the Rohingyas, and the global response.
